title: Passed On to the Next Generation

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Aaron's sacred garments will belong to his descendants so that they can be anointed and ordained in them. The son who succeeds him as priest and comes to the tent of meeting to minister in the Holy Place is to wear them seven days." - Exodus 29:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sacred garments do not go into a grave with Aaron. They pass to his descendants, worn by the son who succeeds him. God was already thinking beyond the first generation. The ministry would continue, and the means of it would be handed on.

There is wisdom in this for anyone who serves God. We are not building something that must end with us. Whatever God has entrusted to you — faith, understanding, ministry, a household of prayer — is meant to be handed forward. The question is not only "am I serving faithfully?" but "who am I preparing to carry this after me?"

Paul instructed Timothy to entrust what he had heard to reliable people who would also be qualified to teach others (2 Tim 2:2) — four generations in a single sentence. And Psalm 78 speaks of telling the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the Lord, so that they in turn would tell their children (Ps 78:4-6). Who is watching how you follow God? What are you deliberately passing on? The garments were made to outlast the man who first wore them.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Who is God asking me to invest in and hand something on to?
Am I building something that will outlast me, or only serving for now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, what You have given me was never meant to stop with me. Show me who to invest in, and help me faithfully hand on what I have received. Amen.
